questions.prompt: What is the safest way to choose TypeScript compiler settings?
options: Disable all strict options before inspecting diagnostics.
Align the configuration with the installed compiler, target runtime, libraries and bundler, then type-check the project.
Copy a tsconfig from another project without checking its runtime.
Assume every option works in every TypeScript version.
questions.answer_key: Align the configuration with the installed compiler, target runtime, libraries and bundler, then type-check the project.
questions.explanation: Compiler settings describe environment assumptions and change across versions; validate migration and build behavior.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Incremental Builds”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with build information files and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with build information files and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Build information files”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Incremental Builds”?
options: Assume comparing incremental and clean builds is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check avoiding unnecessary work, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check avoiding unnecessary work, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Avoiding unnecessary work”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
